name: Uganda Bird Guides Club

guide_vetting.detail: Around 80 professional bird guides trained through the club, whose founder Herbert Byaruhanga is BirdLife International's accredited guide trainer for East Africa. The associated Uganda Women Birders network has trained over 100 women, with around 30 now earning income as guides.

conservation.detail: Guide training as a conservation livelihood programme across Uganda's birding sites.

blurb: The association behind most of Uganda's professional bird guides, from the shoebill swamps of Mabamba to the Albertine Rift endemics of Bwindi.

name: BirdLife South Africa Community Bird Guides

guide_vetting.detail: Running since 2001, the programme has trained over 200 people from rural communities as professional bird guides, with around 50 active guides today, supported by BirdLife South Africa and Swarovski Optik.

conservation.detail: Community guide training that turns birding tourism into rural livelihoods across South Africa's birding routes.

blurb: BirdLife South Africa's vetted community guides cover the country's great birding routes, bookable directly through the programme's guide directory.

name: Northern Colombia Birding Trail Guides

guide_vetting.body: Audubon, Asociacion Calidris and Patrimonio Natural
guide_vetting.detail: More than 30 local guides trained along the Northern Colombia Birding Trail through a partnership between Audubon, Asociacion Calidris, Patrimonio Natural and USAID, including Wayuu community members in La Guajira.

conservation.detail: Trail-based community guiding that keeps tourism income in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and Caribbean coast communities.

blurb: Trained local guides along the trail that links the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the Perija foothills and the Guajira desert, home to dozens of endemics.

name: Mitu Community Bird Guides

guide_vetting.detail: Indigenous Tucano community guides in Mitu trained through the Etno-Aves Vaupes programme with local biologists, guiding the white-sand and terra firme specialties of the Colombian Amazon.

conservation.detail: Community-owned guiding in indigenous territory where birding income supports Tucano communities directly.

blurb: Indigenous guides in Colombia's Vaupes, where some of the Amazon's most wanted species are found with the people who know the forest best.

name: Kiunga Nature Tours
location: Kiunga, Western Province, Papua New Guinea

guide_vetting.detail: Run by Samuel Kepuknai with village communities in Western Province, the region that holds more than half of Papua New Guinea's bird diversity. Guiding here is village based, and nearly all birding access runs through local guides.

conservation.detail: Village-based birding tourism that channels income to landowner communities around Kiunga and Tabubil.

blurb: The gateway to birds-of-paradise country: village-based guiding around Kiunga, where local knowledge is the only way to the display trees.
